comments.content: Trimming the `sha256:` prefix globally means the bar label now embeds the full 64-char digest (e.g. `pulling <64 hex chars>...`) instead of the previously truncated 12 chars. `progress.Bar.String()` sizes the bar as `termWidth - pre.Len() - suf.Len() - 5` without clipping the message (`messageWidth` defaults to -1), so a ~75-char label plus suffix far exceeds an 80-column terminal. The line wraps, and `Progress.render()`'s cursor-up bookkeeping (`p.pos`) then corrupts the display on every 100ms redraw. Truncate to a short prefix after trimming while keeping the guard against short/non-digest values (e.g. when the server sends a model name as the digest).

comments.content:
Treating any existing file of the expected size as complete, combined with in-place writes without `O_TRUNC`, can silently accept a corrupted blob.

`Put` writes chunks at absolute offsets (`io.NewOffsetWriter(c.f, chunk.Start)`) and nothing is truncated/removed when a write fails. If a previous pull fails on an early chunk but later chunks (higher offsets) were written, the file ends up exactly `size` bytes with a hole. Both this check and `Registry.Pull`'s `exists` (size-only) then consider the layer cached, the manifest is linked, and the corrupted blob is served for that digest.

`Chunker.digest`/`size` are stored but never read, so `Close` performs no whole-blob validation (each `checkWriter` only validates a single chunk). Suggest verifying the assembled blob against `c.digest`/`c.size` (e.g. via the newly added `Digest.Sum`) before reporting success, and truncating/removing the file when a `Put` fails. Also consider validating `chunk.Start`/`chunk.End` against `c.size` so a bad chunksums response cannot grow the file past the expected size.

comments.content:
The error yielded by the `chunksums` iterator is only reported to the trace and then dropped: `break` exits the loop, and `g.Wait()` below only sees errors from the chunk goroutines. If the chunksums endpoint fails or returns a truncated list, `Pull` continues on to store the manifest and `Link` the model, then returns `nil` — i.e. a successful pull with a partially written/missing layer (and, because `Chunker` writes directly into the final blob path, potentially a wrong-content blob that already matches `l.Size`). The same silent-success pattern applies to the `c.Chunked` failure above (`t.update(l, 0, err); continue`), which skips a layer on disk errors. Note `Trace.Update` implementations (e.g. `server/internal/registry/server.go`) ignore the `err` argument, so nothing else observes these failures either.

Capture the error and return it after `g.Wait()`, e.g.:

These blob GETs are built with `http.NewRequestWithContext`, bypassing `r.newRequest`, which is what sets `User-Agent` and the signed `Authorization: Bearer ...` token derived from `Registry.Key`. The chunksums request above does use `r.newRequest`, and the previous implementation cloned the already-signed request, so chunk downloads used to be authenticated. After this change every chunk request goes out unauthenticated and pulls of private/authenticated models will fail with 401/403.

`defer chunked.Close()` is registered inside the per-layer loop, so every layer's blob file stays open until `Pull` returns (file-descriptor pressure for models with many layers) and the `Close` error is discarded on every return path. Since the chunked writer writes straight to the final blob path, a failed close/flush is reported as success and partial data is left in the cache. Close the writer explicitly once the layer's chunks have finished and propagate the error — e.g. move the per-layer download body into its own function that `defer`s/returns `chunked.Close()`.

Chunk sizing is now driven entirely by the server's chunksums response, but `Registry.MaxChunkSize` (lines ~216-220) and its `maxChunkSize()` accessor were left behind: the field is still public and documented as "If zero, the default is [DefaultMaxChunkSize]" while `DefaultMaxChunkSize` no longer exists, and the `Pull` doc comment still refers to `[Registry.MaxChunkSize]`. The knob is silently ignored now (`registry_test.go` even sets `rc.MaxChunkSize = 3` expecting smaller chunks). Please remove the field and fix the stale doc references.

`Put` never validates the chunk range against the size declared to `Chunked` (`c.size` is set but never read). Chunk ranges come from the registry's chunksums response, so an out-of-range `chunk.Start`/`chunk.End` is written past the intended blob extent via `io.NewOffsetWriter`, silently extending the file beyond `size` (and `Get` only rejects zero-length files, so it will be treated as a valid blob). Boundary cases also slip through: `chunk.Size()` can overflow to a negative value (e.g. `End == math.MaxInt64`), in which case `io.CopyN` returns `(0, nil)` and the digest is never verified; a zero-size chunk likewise skips the hash check entirely. Reject out-of-bounds chunks before writing.
